stem: In a healthy mammalian heart, contraction of the four chambers is coordinated by the action of the sinoatrial node (SAN) and atrioventricular node (AVN).

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
After the atria fill with blood, atrial systole (contraction) occurs.

State the events that occur to initiate and cause atrial systole.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: State **and** explain how the structure of the heart allows the atria to contract before the ventricles.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
Fig. 2.1 shows blood pressure changes that occur in the left ventricle, left atrium and aorta during one cardiac cycle.

**E, F, G and H** are the points at which a valve opens or closes as a result of blood pressure changes.

{{figure:figure_2_1.png}}

Fig. 2.1
parts.text: For each of the points **E, F, G and H** on Fig. 2.1, name the valve concerned **and** state whether the valve opens or closes.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Explain how Fig. 2.1 provides evidence that the wall of the left atrium has a different thickness to the wall of the left ventricle.
